name: Retrospective role heading
does: Titles the role file

name: Retrospective identity, mine the run
does: Fresh-context subagent mines the accepted run for durable guidance improvements as minimal edits
preventsClaim: the same correction recurring in a future run
costNote: 1 retrospective per accepted run, unless Retrospective: off

name: Propose only, never edit
does: Propose only; never edit a file

name: Never propose plugin file edits
does: Never propose an edit to the mise plugin's own files
preventsClaim: a project run rewriting the shared workflow

name: Dispatch names mise dir and config
does: Dispatch prompt names the mise directory and the mise config

name: Sources heading
does: Section heading

name: Read in order framing
does: Introduces the ordered source list

name: Read friction and progress logs
does: Read the friction log, which may be absent, and the progress log, its Deviations entries especially

name: Read the run artifacts
does: Read goals.md, requirements.md when present, and the plan overview

name: Read the branch commits
does: Read the branch commits; fix commits and rework name friction the logs miss
preventsClaim: friction that was never logged going unnoticed
costNote: git log over the branch

name: Read the governing guidance verbatim
does: Read config, Checklist, CLAUDE.md and every Skills and guides doc; propose against actual text
preventsClaim: proposing an edit to text that does not exist
costNote: reads every registered guide, unbounded by project size

name: Corrections framing
does: Introduces the correction-source list

name: Correction source: friction log lines
does: Treat correction: and acceptance: user flagged lines in the friction log as corrections
preventsClaim: a user correction not turning into a proposal

name: Correction source: UI Tweaks Log
does: Treat the UI Tweaks Log in mocks.context.md as corrections when the run mocked
preventsClaim: a user correction not turning into a proposal

name: Correction source: user commits
does: Treat user-authored commits after the last mise: task done, by subject prefix, as corrections; read their diffs
preventsClaim: a user correction not turning into a proposal
costNote: git log plus a diff read per user commit

name: Correction source: external review notes
does: Follow the config Review notes section verbatim; every reviewer turn there is a correction
preventsClaim: a user correction not turning into a proposal
costNote: reads an external notes file per the named contract

name: What counts as a finding heading
does: Section heading

name: Every correction yields a proposal
does: Every correction yields a proposal; none is dropped; route each to one of three kinds
costNote: proposal count scales with corrections; each needs a user adopt/reject decision

name: Route: checklist edit, 15-rule cap
does: Propose a checklist edit for an ignored well-placed rule or a mechanical diff-checkable rule; sharpen or merge at the cap
preventsClaim: a rule that lives in a doc and is still ignored recurring

name: Route: durable doc
does: Propose a durable doc for a product or design decision or a genuinely new convention, with a registration line
preventsClaim: a decision lost after cleanup deletes the mise directory

name: Route: config edit or plugin candidate
does: Route a correction about the workflow's own approach to the config-edit or plugin-candidate route

name: Bar for non-correction findings
does: Every other finding needs a concrete incident from this run that a specific guidance edit would have prevented

name: Target: an existing guide
does: Route the incident to an existing guide whose scope covers it

name: Target: the mise config
does: Route a wrong or missing config value: test exceptions, mock conditions, quality commands
preventsClaim: a mis-set config repeating the same friction

name: Target: CLAUDE.md
does: Route a repo-wide code convention to CLAUDE.md

name: Target: a new doc, with conditions
does: Propose a new doc only when a critical lesson has no home; give content plus registration line and a crisp when-to-use

name: Target: plugin candidate
does: Describe a flaw in how the stages ran as a plugin candidate for the user to take upstream
preventsClaim: a workflow flaw edited into project guidance

name: Target: nothing, drop it
does: Drop a finding that fits no target

name: Rules framing
does: Introduces the proposal rules

name: Proposals are minimal diffs
does: Proposals are minimal diffs; deleting or consolidating existing guidance counts

name: One incident must matter
does: One incident justifies a proposal only if ignoring it would plausibly damage a future run
preventsClaim: one-off noise codified as a rule

name: Group by pattern with provenance
does: Group proposals by pattern; each carries a Covers or Incident line; never a cosmetic wording preference

name: Empty report is a success
does: An empty report is a success when there were no corrections and nothing cleared the bar

name: Reporting back heading
does: Section heading

name: Number the proposals
does: Introduces the numbered proposal template

name: Proposal template
does: Fixed shape: target file, kind, exact Edit text, Covers, Incident
preventsClaim: a proposal too vague to apply verbatim
costNote: proposals return into the orchestrator context for the adopt prompt

name: Recommend adopt line
does: End with Recommend: adopt numbers, naming only proposals worth staking a future run on
preventsClaim: the user adjudicating doubtful proposals unaided
costNote: feeds the adopt/reject prompt at the second human gate

name: Exact no-proposals sentence
does: With no proposals, report one exact sentence

name: Report goes to orchestrator
does: States the final message audience

name: Do not heading
does: Section heading for the sanctioned-redundancy list

name: Do not edit any file
does: Never edit a file; the orchestrator applies what the user adopts
costNote: restatement of the identity line

name: Do not propose plugin edits
does: Never propose edits to the mise plugin's skill or instruction files; workflow flaws are report-only
preventsClaim: a project run rewriting the shared workflow
costNote: restatement of the identity line

name: Reviewer role heading
does: Titles the role file

name: Reviewer identity, never fixes
does: Fresh-context reviewer checks one task's committed work and reports defects, never fixing them
preventsClaim: an author reviewing their own work
costNote: 1 reviewer per task, re-run after each fix round

name: Read task, commits, config, log, guides
does: Read task file, commit hashes, config, progress log, git show per commit, Checklist, matching guides
costNote: git show per commit plus 4+ file reads per reviewer spawn

name: What to check heading
does: Section heading

name: Task-spec requirements missed
does: Check for task-spec requirements the diff misses
preventsClaim: a task marked done without doing what it specified

name: Guides entries not followed
does: Check the task Guides entries the work does not follow

name: Bugs, security holes, debug code
does: Check correctness bugs, security holes and leftover debug code

name: Missing test coverage
does: Check missing test coverage no Test exception cited in the task file excuses

name: Two-pass: review documenter prose
does: In two-pass mode review the documenter's comments, docstrings and markdown docs in the named commits

name: User copy vs goals and mocks
does: Check user-facing copy that departs from the approved goals and mocks
preventsClaim: invented copy diverging from what the user approved

name: Verify checklist answers in commits
does: Merge answers across commits, confirm each pass against the diff, answer every n-a itself; wrong answers are defects
preventsClaim: a missed rule hiding behind an n-a answer
costNote: reviewer re-answers up to 15 rules per task

name: No checklist line at all
does: Report when no commit carries a Checklist line
preventsClaim: a task shipped without its self-review answers

name: Reporting back heading
does: Section heading

name: Report only the four failure kinds
does: Report only correctness, task-spec, guide and checklist failures as concrete defects; ignore cosmetic nits
preventsClaim: a reviewer asked for gaps reporting some even when work is sound

name: Tag prose vs not-prose
does: Tag each defect prose or not-prose so the orchestrator routes it to the right fixer
preventsClaim: a prose defect sent to the implementer, or the reverse
costNote: each tag class can spawn its own fix subagent

name: Nothing to report is exactly none
does: Report exactly none when there is nothing to report
preventsClaim: an ambiguous report triggering a fix round

name: Report goes to orchestrator
does: States the final message audience

name: Config reference heading
does: Titles the reference

name: Setup writes a minimal values-only config
does: Setup interviews the user and writes only applicable sections as values, no instructional prose
preventsClaim: config bloat, since every stage and every subagent reads the file
costNote: config is loaded into the driver and every subagent spawn

name: Never restate consumption rules
does: Never restate consumption rules here or in the generated config; they belong to the reading files

name: Generated file shape heading
does: Section heading

name: Worked config example
does: Full example config showing every section in place
costNote: 55 lines loaded into the setup stage context

name: Section reference heading
does: Section heading

name: Required sections framing
does: Marks the following four knobs as required

name: Knob: Mise directory
does: Where in-flight work lives, suggested .mise/, holding stage artifacts and .workflow-state only
preventsClaim: stray files making the directory's existence an unreliable in-flight signal

name: Knob: Branch convention
does: One line naming work branches with a slug placeholder

name: Knob: Checklist
does: Path to the review checklist; Code then Prose, numbered continuously, diff-answerable, cap 15, never blocking
preventsClaim: recurring error classes; an unbounded checklist
costNote: every implementer, documenter, reviewer and acceptance pass answers it

name: Knob: Quality commands
does: Format, Check, Unit tests, optional scoped Task tests; each slot one command or an ordered list; run commands only
preventsClaim: confusing how tests are run with how they are written
costNote: defines every command the workflow runs

name: Optional sections, prefer pointers
does: Omit sections that do not apply; use a pointer to an existing doc whenever the content already lives in the project
preventsClaim: duplicated project guidance drifting from its source

name: Knob: Mock conditions
does: Conditions deciding whether a feature gets an HTML mock; matching any takes the full route
costNote: a match adds the mock stage and its iteration loop at the goals gate

name: Knob: Mock guidance
does: How mocks should look: product name, UI code root, look-and-feel notes

name: Knob: Test conventions
does: Authoring conventions: where each kind of test lives, naming, frameworks, fixtures

name: Knob: Test exceptions
does: condition — alternative verification entries; the method changes, verification never disappears
preventsClaim: verification vanishing where a test is impractical

name: Knob: Skills and guides
does: One entry per line as name (skill or doc, optionally required): when to use; required must never be bypassed
preventsClaim: a mandatory runner or style guide bypassed
costNote: every matching entry is read by each role that matches it

name: Knob: Models
does: Per-role model for seven roles, default session; a documenter line switches two-pass mode on
preventsClaim: paying session-model cost for every generation role
costNote: a documenter line adds one subagent per task and per later code commit

name: Knob: Database migrations
does: The migration generation command, if the project has one

name: Knob: Backlog
does: Freeform instructions for fetching top to-do items from an external tracker; read verbatim
costNote: an external tracker call when starting new work

name: Knob: Review notes
does: Freeform instructions for reading the user's external review notes for the branch; read verbatim
costNote: read once by the retrospective

name: Knob: Retrospective off
does: Only ever written as Retrospective: off; omitting the line keeps the retrospective on
costNote: off removes 1 subagent per run

name: Knob: Ship
does: pr, merge with a recorded style, or off; omitting the line makes the close-out ask each time
preventsClaim: assuming a merge style the user never chose
costNote: omitted value adds a question at close-out
